newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKET - Kookmin's FRN surfaces.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKET - Kookmin's FRN surfaces.

text.p: Kookmin Bank's US$200 million subordinated floating rate note issue offered some excitement on the otherwise dull Asian debt market on Monday.

Callable in year five, the 10-year paper were launched at par and re-offered at 99.872 on Monday morning. They pay a quarterly coupon of 60 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) for years one through five and LIBOR plus 185 basis points thereafter.
It give a re-offer yield of LIBOR plus 63 basis points payable quarterly for years one through five and LIBOR plus 122.5 basis points for years one through 10.
Fees are 32.5 basis points split as 20 basis points for selling and 12.5 basis points for management underwriting.
The issue is expected to obtain Baa1 by Moody's, said the lead managers Chase Manhattan Asia and Merrill Lynch Far East.
That's even tighter than what Korea Exchange Bank paid for its simlarly structured deal launched in late October this year.

Also callable after five years, the A3-rated 10-year subordinated floating rate note was launched at par and re-offered at 99.95. It pays a quarterly coupon of 64 basis points over LIBOR for years one through five, and 200 basis points thereafter. Its re-offer yield is Libor plus 65 basis points payable quarterly for years one through five and Libor plus 132.5 basis points for years one through 10, a lot more generous than the Baa1-expected Kookmin issue.
Traders explained Kookmin's confidence in its own issue, noticeable in its thin pricing, is bolstered by KEB paper's outstanding performance in secondary market.
The KEB's subordinated issue is one of the very few Korean paper capable of being traded above par, one trader said.
"But timing is another reason. Kookmin tries to hit while the iron is still hot." the trader added.
Kookmin's issue is expected to be scooped up by bankers hunting for long-term high grade paper to fill their quotas before the year ends.
